item.title: I made a WordPress theme that looks like iOS
item.description:
I’ve been staring at my iPhone all day and I got tired of how every WordPress blog looks the same – flat headers, generic sidebars, the whole deal. So I spent the evening building a theme that actually looks like iOS, and I’m putting it up for anyone who wants it.

The whole thing is built around that familiar iOS table view look. Striped background, rounded white cells with the little chevron arrows, a search bar at the top that matches the system aesthetic. It’s not trying to be a 1:1 copy of the iPhone – it’s just borrowing enough of the visual language that people who spend their days in iOS will feel at home.

item.title: Black & Blue — a free PSD template
item.description:
This is a template I designed for Zap Web Online — a web solutions company that wanted a dark, techy look. The brief was fairly open: make it look fast, modern, and a bit futuristic. Hence the name.

The layout is a fixed-width centre column on a textured metallic background. The header has the Zap Web logo on the left, a four-item navigation bar (Home, About Us, Portfolio, Contact) with blue highlight on the active tab, and a “Chat Live” button tucked into the top right of the banner. The banner itself is a glowing blue waveform against a black gradient with the tagline “Lightning Fast Web Solutions”.

item.title: Backdrop for Udbhav 2010
item.description:
Udbhav is an annual cultural festival that brings together students through music, dance, and creative expression. For the 2010 edition, I designed another stage backdrop – this time with a slightly different approach to the visual language.

The backdrop needed to function as the stage’s focal point while leaving room for the performances. It had to read clearly from the back of the venue, carry energy without overwhelming the stage, and fit the overall visual identity I was building for Udbhav that year.

item.title: Book Cover for Udbhav 2009 Souvenir
item.description:
Along with the posters, flyers, and backdrop for Udbhav 2009, I designed the cover for the event souvenir book. The brief was straightforward: something that felt cohesive with the rest of the visual identity while standing on its own as a keepsake.

This was part of a larger design effort for Udbhav 2009 that also included posters, flyers, stickers, mini banners, and the stage backdrop.

item.title: Backdrop for Udbhav 2009
item.description:
Udbhav is an annual cultural festival that brings together students through music, dance, and creative expression. For the 2009 edition, I was asked to design a backdrop – a large-scale visual piece that would serve as the stage’s focal point.

The challenge was to create something that felt both festive and contemporary. The design needed to work from a distance, communicate energy, and complement the performances happening in front of it without competing for attention.

item.title: Posters for Udbhav 2009
item.description: A set of posters for Udbhav 2009. The goal was to build a visual identity that felt fresh and energetic, something that would stand out on notice boards and social media alike. Each poster uses a different colour way but shares the same typography and layout so they read as a family.

item.title: Udbhav 2009 Stickers
item.description:
Stickers for Udbhav 2009. Small format, but they need to carry the same visual identity as everything else. Designing at this scale means every detail has to earn its place — there’s no room for clutter.

This was part of a larger design effort for Udbhav 2009 that also included posters, flyers, mini banners, the souvenir book cover, the participation certificate, and the stage backdrop.

item.description:

This was part of a larger design effort for Udbhav 2009 that also included posters, flyers, stickers, mini banners, the souvenir book cover, and the stage backdrop.

item.title: Mini Banners for Udbhav 2009 Events

This was part of a larger design effort for Udbhav 2009 that also included posters, flyers, stickers, the souvenir book cover, and the stage backdrop.

item.title: Participation Certificate for Respograph 2009
item.description: A participation certificate design for Respograph 2009. The challenge with certificates is balancing formality with visual interest — they need to feel official without looking like every other template.

item.title: Logos for Computer Science and Engineering Association
item.description:
The Computer Science and Engineering Association at Aurora University needed a new logo, so they put out a call for designs. I submitted some entries.

What follows is the full range of my “talent” on display, from “I can see the vision” to “what were you thinking”.

I really wanted them to know that the C.S.E. Association rocks. I also couldn’t spell “officially”. The logo reads “WE OFICIALLY ROCK” around a circle with “C.S.E.” in the middle and “A.S.T.R.A.” at the bottom. The typo does most of the work here.

item.title: A modern black on wood website template for any business or personal portfolio
item.description:
I put together a simple website template that uses a dark color scheme over a wood texture background. It is meant to be flexible enough for any kind of business site or personal portfolio.

The design is straightforward. A navigation bar sits at the top, followed by a main content area and a sidebar on the right. The wood texture gives it warmth without being distracting, and the white text on it reads fine on most screens.

item.title: Cover Design for ASTRA College Magazine
item.description:
I was asked to put together a cover for ASTRA, the college magazine. The brief was loose enough that I could experiment with typography and layout without worrying too much about brand guidelines or committee sign-off.

The main challenge was making the masthead work at different scales. College magazines tend to be printed cheaply on decent paper, so the design needed to hold up even when the press wasn’t perfect. I kept the palette simple and let the type carry the weight.
